note: Printed claims only (Phase 5 Step 6). Covers Book I Answers 13, 14 and 15, the only image-verified answers (programs.md N-5; image-read again here from book1.pdf PDF p.33 = printed p.31: Answer 13 is 6+/6Y 6X/6A 6B/6- 6X/D17 D18/M-, Answer 14 is 5+/5Y 5Z/6X 6Y/D17 M-/D18, Answer 15 is 6+/6X 6Y/D17 M-/D18 D18/5X 5Y/D19; Answer 15 is five lines in full, and its diagram draws 5Z but wires nothing to it). The three answers share no wiring, so one fixture carries all three: wires and as_printed are Answer 13's printed list (cords 0-4); with power off the script disconnects them and connects Answer 14 (cords 5-8), then Answer 15 (cords 9-13), as hole-ended connect commands. No erratum touches Answers 13-15 (ER-03 is prose for Problems 7 and 18), so errata_applied is empty. Before Answers 14 and 15 the operator sets the pointer knob back to 0 by hand (dialGrab to 0, power off); that reset and the c0 starting position are script choices, not printed. Asserted: Answer 13, after pushbutton 6 is pushed, light 6 on and the dial turning (until c8, reached in either direction within one revolution, so direction is not asserted). Answers 14 and 15, Problem 14's statement: with pushbutton 6 up and pushbutton 5 up, with pushbutton 6 up and pushbutton 5 down, and with both down (pb5 pushed first, then pb6), the dial is still at c0 after a 600 ms window (more than one pad pitch at 25 rpm, less than one revolution at 90 rpm, so a turning dial cannot pass); then with pushbutton 5 released and pushbutton 6 still down, the dial turns (until c8). Not asserted: Problem 13's converse (dial still and light 6 off with pushbutton 6 up) is not printed; pushing pushbutton 5 while the dial is already turning under pushbutton 6 is covered by 'when both ... are down', but asserting that the dial stays still afterwards needs the rest position after the invented STOP-short coast, so it is left to Step 7; direction of rotation and stop positions are not printed. Answers 1-12 and 16-20 stay out: OCR only, not image-verified. Rotary geometry, run rate, coast and fitted motor resistances remain profile fallbacks O-R1, O-R3 and O-R5; until windows are sized for a run rate as slow as 25 rpm.
